title: Prakrama 2, Sarga 7. Grace to the Devotees
html:
The appearance of the dancing Lord; the meaning of Srivasa's name; Murari's "Ramashtaka" and the name "Ramadasa"; service to Srivasa as worship of the Lord; Narayani receives the remnants of His meal

Verse 1

सितनवांशुकमस्तकवेष्टन-
स्तरुणविद्रुमसन्निभहारधृक्।
वरभुजद्युतिरञ्जितकङ्कणः
स्फुटनवीनसरोजकरो बभौ॥१॥

sitanavāṁśukamastakaveṣṭana-
staruṇavidrumasannibhahāradhṛk|
varabhujadyutirañjitakaṅkaṇaḥ
sphuṭanavīnasarojakaro babhau||1||

sita-nava-amshuka-mastaka-veshtanah — His head wrapped in new white cloth; taruna-vidruma-sannibha-hara-dhrik — wearing a necklace like young coral; vara-bhuja-dyuti-ranjita-kankanah — His bracelets tinted by the splendour of His fine arms; sphuta-navina-saroja-karah — His hands like freshly opened lotuses; babhau — shone.

1His head was wrapped in new white cloth; He wore a necklace like young coral; His bracelets were tinted by the splendour of His fine arms, and His hands were like freshly opened lotuses — and He shone.

Verse 2

चलचेलनिबद्धधटीधरो-
ऽरुणबहिर्वसनो नटवेशधृक्।
वरनितम्बविलम्बितबाहु[…]
वरविलम्बिनागपतिः स्फुटम्॥२॥

calacelanibaddhadhaṭīdharo-
'ruṇabahirvasano naṭaveśadhṛk|
varanitambavilambitabāhu[…]
varavilambināgapatiḥ sphuṭam||2||

chala-chela-nibaddha-dhati-dharah — wearing a loincloth bound with a fluttering cloth; aruna-bahir-vasanah — in a crimson outer garment; nata-vesha-dhrik — in a dancer's attire; vara-nitamba-vilambita-bahu — His arms hanging to His fine hips; vara-vilambi-naga-patih — (like) the lord of serpents; sphutam — plainly.

2He wore a loincloth bound with a fluttering cloth, a crimson outer garment and a dancer's attire, and His arms, hanging down to His fine hips, plainly resembled the king of serpents1.

Verse 3

चरणपङ्कजरञ्जितनूपुरो
वरनखद्युतिरञ्जितशीतगुः।
पदतलद्युतिरञ्जितविद्रुमो
द्रुतसुवर्णरुचिः शनकैर्व्रजन्॥३॥

caraṇapaṅkajarañjitanūpuro
varanakhadyutirañjitaśītaguḥ|
padataladyutirañjitavidrumo
drutasuvarṇaruciḥ śanakairvrajan||3||

charana-pankaja-ranjita-nupurah — His anklets graced by His lotus feet; vara-nakha-dyuti-ranjita-shitaguh — the moon tinted by the splendour of His fine nails; pada-tala-dyuti-ranjita-vidrumah — coral tinted by the glow of His soles; druta-suvarna-ruchih — with the lustre of molten gold; shanakaih — slowly; vrajan — walking.

3Anklets were graced by His lotus feet; the splendour of His lovely nails tinted the moon, the glow of His soles tinted coral; shining like molten gold, He moved with slow steps.

Verse 4

परिननर्त लसन्मुखपङ्कजो
निजजनैर्निजनामपरायणैः।
मधुरिपोर्मधुगीतसुगायनैः
सुरगणैर्दिवि देवपतिर्यथा॥४॥

parinanarta lasanmukhapaṅkajo
nijajanairnijanāmaparāyaṇaiḥ|
madhuripormadhugītasugāyanaiḥ
suragaṇairdivi devapatiryathā||4||

parinanarta — danced all around; lasat-mukha-pankajah — His lotus face shining; nija-janaih — with His own people; nija-nama-parayanaih — devoted to His name; madhuripoh — of the Enemy of Madhu; madhu-gita-su-gayanaih — sweet singers of honeyed songs; sura-ganaih — with the hosts of gods; divi — in heaven; deva-patih — the lord of the gods; yatha — as.

4He danced, His lotus face aglow, while around Him His own people, devoted to His name, sweetly sang the honeyed songs of the Enemy of Madhu — as the lord of the gods dances in heaven amid the hosts of the gods.

Verse 5

करयुगाहतसाधुसुमन्दिरा-
रवसुधा वसुधातलवासिनाम्।
मुदमधात्कलकण्ठरवान्विता
सुमनसामनिशं कमलापतेः॥५॥

karayugāhatasādhusumandirā-
ravasudhā vasudhātalavāsinām|
mudamadhātkalakaṇṭharavānvitā
sumanasāmaniśaṁ kamalāpateḥ||5||

kara-yuga-ahata-sadhu-su-mandira-rava-sudha — the nectar of the ringing of fine mandiras struck by both hands; vasudha-tala-vasinam — to those dwelling on the earth; mudam — joy; adhat — gave; kala-kantha-rava-anvita — joined with sweet-voiced song; sumanasam — to the good-hearted; anisham — unceasingly; kamala-pateh — of the Lord of Kamala.

5The nectar of the ringing of fine mandiras struck by both hands of the Lord of Kamala, joined with sweet-voiced singing, unceasingly gave joy to the good-hearted dwelling on earth.

Verse 6

उपविशन्नवकम्बलसंवृते
हरिहरोऽत्र विचित्रो रराम।
सुरगृहे निजलोकसमावृते
वरद आववृधे निजतेजसा॥६॥

upaviśannavakambalasaṁvṛte
hariharo'tra vicitro rarāma|
suragṛhe nijalokasamāvṛte
varada āvavṛdhe nijatejasā||6||

upavishan — sitting down; nava-kambala-samvrite — on (a seat) covered with a new blanket; hari-harah — Harihara; atra — here; vichitrah — wondrous; rarama — took delight; sura-grihe — in the temple; nija-loka-samavrite — surrounded by His own people; varadah — the Giver of boons; avavridhe — grew; nija-tejasa — with His own radiance.

6Then the wondrous Harihara2 sat down here on a seat covered with a new blanket and took delight; and in the temple, surrounded by His own people, the Giver of boons grew in His own radiance.

Verse 7

ततः प्रोवाच श्रीवासं मधुरं मधुसूदनः।
श्रीभक्तिरस्या वासस्त्वमतः श्रीवास उच्यते॥७॥

tataḥ provāca śrīvāsaṁ madhuraṁ madhusūdanaḥ|
śrībhaktirasyā vāsastvamataḥ śrīvāsa ucyate||7||

tatah — then; provacha — said; shrivasam — to Srivasa; madhuram — sweetly; madhusudanah — Madhusudana; shri-bhaktih — the beauteous devotion (Shri); asyah — her; vasah — the abode; tvam — you; atah — therefore; shri-vasah — Srivasa; uchyate — you are called.

7Then Madhusudana said sweetly to Srivasa: "Shri is devotion, and you are her abode; that is why you are called Srivasa."

Verse 8

गोपीनाथमिदं प्राह त्वं मे दास इति स्मृतः॥८॥

gopīnāthamidaṁ prāha tvaṁ me dāsa iti smṛtaḥ||8||

gopinatham — to Gopinatha; idam — this; praha — said; tvam — you; me — My; dasah — servant; iti — thus; smritah — are known.

8And to Gopinatha3 He said: "You are known as My servant."

Verse 9

ततः प्रोवाच करुणो मुरारिं तां पठ स्वयम्।
कवितां भवतः श्रुत्वा स पपाठ शुभाक्षरम्॥९॥

tataḥ provāca karuṇo murāriṁ tāṁ paṭha svayam|
kavitāṁ bhavataḥ śrutvā sa papāṭha śubhākṣaram||9||

tatah — then; provacha — said; karunah — the Compassionate; murarim — to Murari; tam — that; patha — recite; svayam — yourself; kavitam — poem; bhavatah — of yours; shrutva — hearing; sah — he; papatha — recited; shubha-aksharam — in lovely syllables.

9Then the Compassionate One said to Murari: "Recite that poem of yours yourself."4 Hearing this, he recited it in lovely syllables:

The Eight Verses

Verse 10

राजत्किरीटमणिदीधितिदीपिताश-
मुद्यद्बृहस्पतिकविप्रतिमे वहन्तम्।
द्वे कुण्डलेऽङ्करहितेन्दुसमानवक्त्रं
रामं जगत्त्रयगुरुं सततं भजामि॥१०॥

rājatkirīṭamaṇidīdhitidīpitāśa-
mudyadbṛhaspatikavipratime vahantam|
dve kuṇḍale'ṅkarahitendusamānavaktraṁ
rāmaṁ jagattrayaguruṁ satataṁ bhajāmi||10||

rajat-kirita-mani-didhiti-dipita-asham — who lights up the quarters with the rays of the gems of His gleaming crown; udyat-brihaspati-kavi-pratime — resembling the rising Brihaspati and Kavi; vahantam — wearing; dve — two; kundale — earrings; anka-rahita-indu-samana-vaktram — whose face is like a spotless moon; ramam — Rama; jagat-traya-gurum — the teacher of the three worlds; satatam — ever; bhajami — I worship.

10"The rays of the gems of His gleaming crown light up the quarters; He wears earrings like the rising Brihaspati and Kavi5; His face is like a spotless moon. Rama, the teacher of the three worlds, I worship ever.

Verse 11

उद्यद्विभाकरमरीचिविबोधिताब्ज-
नेत्रं सुबिम्बदशनच्छदचारुनासम्।
शुभ्रांशुरश्मिपरिनिर्जितचारुहासं
रामं जगत्त्रयगुरुं सततं भजामि॥११॥

udyadvibhākaramarīcivibodhitābja-
netraṁ subimbadaśanacchadacārunāsam|
śubhrāṁśuraśmiparinirjitacāruhāsaṁ
rāmaṁ jagattrayaguruṁ satataṁ bhajāmi||11||

udyat-vibhakara-marichi-vibodhita-abja-netram — with eyes like lotuses awakened by the rays of the rising sun; su-bimba-dashana-chchhada-charu-nasam — with lips like ripe bimba fruit and a lovely nose; shubhramshu-rashmi-parinirjita-charu-hasam — whose lovely smile outshines the moonbeams; ramam — Rama; jagat-traya-gurum — the teacher of the three worlds; satatam — ever; bhajami — I worship.

11His eyes are like lotuses awakened by the rays of the rising sun; His lips are like ripe bimba fruit, His nose is lovely; His charming smile outshines the moonbeams. Rama, the teacher of the three worlds, I worship ever.

Verse 12

तं कम्बुकण्ठमजमम्बुजतुल्यरूपं
मुक्तावलीकनकहारधृतं विभान्तम्।
विद्युद्बलाकगणसंयुतमम्बुदं वा
रामं जगत्त्रयगुरुं सततं भजामि॥१२॥

taṁ kambukaṇṭhamajamambujatulyarūpaṁ
muktāvalīkanakahāradhṛtaṁ vibhāntam|
vidyudbalākagaṇasaṁyutamambudaṁ vā
rāmaṁ jagattrayaguruṁ satataṁ bhajāmi||12||

tam — Him; kambu-kantham — with a conch-like neck; ajam — the Unborn; ambuja-tulya-rupam — whose form is like a lotus; mukta-avali-kanaka-hara-dhritam — adorned with a string of pearls and a golden necklace; vibhantam — shining; vidyut-balaka-gana-samyutam — with lightning and a flock of cranes; ambudam — a rain-cloud; va — like; ramam — Rama; jagat-traya-gurum — the teacher of the three worlds; satatam — ever; bhajami — I worship.

12His neck is like a conch; the Unborn, His form is like a lotus; adorned with a string of pearls and a golden necklace, He shines like a rain-cloud with lightning and a flock of cranes. Rama, the teacher of the three worlds, I worship ever.

Verse 13

उत्तानहस्ततलसंस्थसहस्रपत्रं
पञ्चच्छदाधिकशतं प्रवराङ्गुलीभिः।
कुर्वत्यशीतकनकद्युति यस्य सीता
पार्श्वेऽस्ति तं रघुवरं सततं भजामि॥१३॥

uttānahastatalasaṁsthasahasrapatraṁ
pañcacchadādhikaśataṁ pravarāṅgulībhiḥ|
kurvatyaśītakanakadyuti yasya sītā
pārśve'sti taṁ raghuvaraṁ satataṁ bhajāmi||13||

uttana-hasta-tala-samstha-sahasra-patram — the thousand-petalled lotus resting on her upturned palm; pancha-chchhada-adhika-shatam — into one of a hundred and five petals; pravara-angulibhih — with her lovely fingers; kurvati — making; ashita-kanaka-dyuti — gleaming like molten gold; yasya — at whose; sita — Sita; parshve — side; asti — is; tam — Him; raghu-varam — the best of the Raghus; satatam — ever; bhajami — I worship.

13At His side is Sita: on her upturned palm rests a thousand-petalled lotus gleaming like molten gold, and her lovely fingers give it five petals more than a hundred6. The best of the Raghus I worship ever.

Verse 14

अग्रे धनुर्धरवरः कनकोज्ज्वलाङ्गो
ज्येष्ठानुसेवनरतो वरभूषणाढ्यः।
शेषाख्यधामवरलक्ष्मण नाम यस्य
रामं जगत्त्रयगुरुं सततं भजामि॥१४॥

agre dhanurdharavaraḥ kanakojjvalāṅgo
jyeṣṭhānusevanarato varabhūṣaṇāḍhyaḥ|
śeṣākhyadhāmavaralakṣmaṇa nāma yasya
rāmaṁ jagattrayaguruṁ satataṁ bhajāmi||14||

agre — in front; dhanur-dhara-varah — the best of bowmen; kanaka-ujjvala-angah — his body bright as gold; jyeshtha-anusevana-ratah — devoted to serving his elder brother; vara-bhushana-adhyah — rich in fine ornaments; shesha-akhya-dhama-vara-lakshmana — the excellent Lakshmana, the abode called Shesha; nama — by name; yasya — of whom; ramam — Rama; jagat-traya-gurum — the teacher of the three worlds; satatam — ever; bhajami — I worship.

14Before Him stands the best of bowmen, his body bright as gold, devoted to serving his elder brother, richly adorned — the excellent Lakshmana, the abode called Shesha7. Rama, the teacher of the three worlds, I worship ever.

Verse 15

यो राघवेन्द्रकुलसिन्धुसुधांशुरूपो
मारीचराक्षससुबाहुमुखान्निहत्य।
यज्ञं ररक्ष कुशिकान्वयपुण्यराशिं
रामं जगत्त्रयगुरुं सततं भजामि॥१५॥

yo rāghavendrakulasindhusudhāṁśurūpo
mārīcarākṣasasubāhumukhānnihatya|
yajñaṁ rarakṣa kuśikānvayapuṇyarāśiṁ
rāmaṁ jagattrayaguruṁ satataṁ bhajāmi||15||

yah — who; raghava-indra-kula-sindhu-sudhamshu-rupah — the moon over the ocean of the dynasty of the Raghu kings; maricha-rakshasa-subahu-mukhan — Maricha and the rakshasas headed by Subahu; nihatya — having slain; yajnam — the sacrifice; raraksha — protected; kushika-anvaya-punya-rashim — the treasure of merit of the line of Kushika; ramam — Rama; jagat-traya-gurum — the teacher of the three worlds; satatam — ever; bhajami — I worship.

15He is the moon over the ocean of the dynasty of the Raghu kings; slaying Maricha and the rakshasas led by Subahu, He protected the sacrifice — the treasure of merit of the line of Kushika8. Rama, the teacher of the three worlds, I worship ever.

Verse 16

हत्वा खरत्रिशिरसौ सगणौ कबन्धं
श्रीदण्डकाननमदूषणमेव कृत्वा।
सुग्रीवमैत्रमकरोद्विनिहत्य शत्रुं
तं राघवं दशमुखान्तकरं भजामि॥१६॥

hatvā kharatriśirasau sagaṇau kabandhaṁ
śrīdaṇḍakānanamadūṣaṇameva kṛtvā|
sugrīvamaitramakarodvinihatya śatruṁ
taṁ rāghavaṁ daśamukhāntakaraṁ bhajāmi||16||

hatva — having slain; khara-trishirasau — Khara and Trishiras; sa-ganau — with their hosts; kabandham — Kabandha; shri-dandaka-kananam — the holy Dandaka forest; adushanam — free of defilement (and of Dushana); eva — indeed; kritva — having made; sugriva-maitram — friendship with Sugriva; akarot — made; vinihatya — having slain; shatrum — the enemy; tam — Him; raghavam — Raghava; dasha-mukha-anta-karam — the slayer of the Ten-headed; bhajami — I worship.

16He slew Khara and Trishiras with their hosts, slew Kabandha, and freed the holy Dandaka forest from defilement — and from Dushana9; slaying Sugriva's enemy, He made friendship with him. Raghava, the slayer of the Ten-headed, I worship.

Verse 17

भङ्क्त्वा पिनाकमकरोज्जनकात्मजाया
वैवाहिकोत्सवविधिं पथि भार्गवेन्द्रम्।
जित्वा पितुर्मुदमुवाह ककुत्स्थवर्यं
रामं जगत्त्रयगुरुं सततं भजामि॥१७॥

bhaṅktvā pinākamakarojjanakātmajāyā
vaivāhikotsavavidhiṁ pathi bhārgavendram|
jitvā piturmudamuvāha kakutsthavaryaṁ
rāmaṁ jagattrayaguruṁ satataṁ bhajāmi||17||

bhanktva — having broken; pinakam — Pinaka (Shiva's bow); akarot — performed; janaka-atmajayah — of Janaka's daughter; vaivahika-utsava-vidhim — the rite of the wedding festival; pathi — on the way; bhargava-indram — the lord of the Bhargavas; jitva — having conquered; pituh — to his father; mudam — joy; uvaha — brought; kakutstha-varyam — the best of Kakutstha's line; ramam — Rama; jagat-traya-gurum — the teacher of the three worlds; satatam — ever; bhajami — I worship.

17Breaking Pinaka, He celebrated His wedding with Janaka's daughter, and on the way home He conquered the lord of the Bhargavas and brought joy to His father10. The best of Kakutstha's line, Rama, the teacher of the three worlds, I worship ever."

Verse 18

इत्थं निशम्य रघुनन्दनराजसिंह-
श्लोकाष्टकं स भगवांश्चरणं मुरारेः।
वैद्यस्य मूर्ध्नि विनिधाय लिलेख भाले
त्वं रामदास इति भो भव मत्प्रसादात्॥१८॥

itthaṁ niśamya raghunandanarājasiṁha-
ślokāṣṭakaṁ sa bhagavāṁścaraṇaṁ murāreḥ|
vaidyasya mūrdhni vinidhāya lilekha bhāle
tvaṁ rāmadāsa iti bho bhava matprasādāt||18||

ittham — thus; nishamya — having heard; raghu-nandana-raja-simha-shloka-ashtakam — the eight verses on the Joy of the Raghus, the lion among kings; sah — He; bhagavan — Bhagavan; charanam — His foot; murareh — of Murari; vaidyasya — the physician; murdhni — on the head; vinidhaya — placing; lilekha — wrote; bhale — on the forehead; tvam — you; rama-dasah — Ramadasa; iti — thus; bhoh — ho; bhava — be; mat-prasadat — by My grace.

18Having heard these eight verses on the Joy of the Raghus, the lion among kings, Bhagavan placed His foot on the head of Murari the physician and wrote on his forehead: "You are Ramadasa."11 "Be so by My grace!"

Verse 19

अपठद्भगवानेकं श्लोकं तच्छृणु मे द्विज॥१९॥

apaṭhadbhagavānekaṁ ślokaṁ tacchṛṇu me dvija||19||

apathat — recited; bhagavan — Bhagavan; ekam — one; shlokam — verse; tat — it; shrinu — hear; me — from me; dvija — O brahmana.

19Then Bhagavan recited a verse — hear it from me, O brahmana12.

Verse 20

न साधयति मां योगो न सांख्यं धर्म उद्धव।
न स्वाध्यायस्तपस्त्यागो यथा भक्तिर्ममोर्जिता॥२०॥

na sādhayati māṁ yogo na sāṁkhyaṁ dharma uddhava|
na svādhyāyastapastyāgo yathā bhaktirmamorjitā||20||

na sadhayati — does not win over; mam — Me; yogah — yoga; na — not; sankhyam — Sankhya; dharmah — dharma; uddhava — O Uddhava; na — not; svadhyayah — Vedic study; tapah — austerity; tyagah — renunciation; yatha — as; bhaktih — devotion; mama — to Me; urjita — mighty.

20"Neither yoga nor Sankhya nor dharma, O Uddhava, neither Vedic study nor austerity nor renunciation win Me over as does mighty devotion to Me."13

Verse 21

पठित्वेदं पुनः प्राह सर्वांस्तत्र समागतान्।
भवद्भिरेव कर्तव्यं श्रीवासस्य विचारणे॥२१॥

paṭhitvedaṁ punaḥ prāha sarvāṁstatra samāgatān|
bhavadbhireva kartavyaṁ śrīvāsasya vicāraṇe||21||

pathitva — having recited; idam — this; punah — then; praha — said; sarvan — to all; tatra — there; samagatan — assembled; bhavadbhih — by you; eva — indeed; kartavyam — is to be done; shrivasasya — of Srivasa; vicharane — according to the judgement.

21Having recited it, He said to all assembled there: "Act according to Srivasa's judgement:

Verse 22

यत्स्यात्तदेव नित्यं वः कुशलं तद्भविष्यति।
श्रीरामपण्डितज्येष्ठभ्रातृसेवा मदर्चना॥२२॥

yatsyāttadeva nityaṁ vaḥ kuśalaṁ tadbhaviṣyati|
śrīrāmapaṇḍitajyeṣṭhabhrātṛsevā madarcanā||22||

yat — whatever; syat — may be (decided); tat eva — that; nityam — always; vah — for you; kushalam — welfare; tat — that; bhavishyati — will be; shri-rama-pandita-jyeshtha-bhratri-seva — service to the elder brother of Sri Rama Pandita; mat-archana — is worship of Me.

22whatever he decides will always be for your good. Service to the elder brother of Sri Rama Pandita is worship of Me.

Verse 23

इति बुद्ध्या विनिश्चित्य कुरु श्रीवाससेवनम्।
तेन ते सकलं भद्रं सदा नित्यं भविष्यति॥२३॥

iti buddhyā viniścitya kuru śrīvāsasevanam|
tena te sakalaṁ bhadraṁ sadā nityaṁ bhaviṣyati||23||

iti — thus; buddhya — with the intellect; vinishchitya — firmly resolving; kuru — perform; shrivasa-sevanam — service to Srivasa; tena — by that; te — for you; sakalam — all; bhadram — good; sada — always; nityam — ever; bhavishyati — will be.

23Grasp this firmly with your understanding and serve Srivasa: by this every blessing will ever be yours."

Verse 24

इत्युक्त्वा हर्षयँल्लोकान्रेमे प्रणतवत्सलः।
भक्तवत्सलतां तस्य दृष्ट्वा सर्वे सुखं ययुः॥२४॥

ityuktvā harṣaya~llokānreme praṇatavatsalaḥ|
bhaktavatsalatāṁ tasya dṛṣṭvā sarve sukhaṁ yayuḥ||24||

iti — thus; uktva — having spoken; harshayan — gladdening; lokan — the people; reme — took delight; pranata-vatsalah — loving to those who bow down; bhakta-vatsalatam — the love for His devotees; tasya — His; drishtva — seeing; sarve — all; sukham — happiness; yayuh — attained.

24So saying, He who loves those who bow to Him took delight in gladdening the people; and all, seeing His love for His devotees, were filled with happiness.

Verse 25

श्रीवासेनार्पितं दुग्धं पूगं माल्यं सधूपकम्।
बुभुजे भगवांस्तत्र शेषान्भृत्याय दत्तवान्॥२५॥

śrīvāsenārpitaṁ dugdhaṁ pūgaṁ mālyaṁ sadhūpakam|
bubhuje bhagavāṁstatra śeṣānbhṛtyāya dattavān||25||

shrivasena — by Srivasa; arpitam — offered; dugdham — milk; pugam — betel; malyam — a garland; sa-dhupakam — with incense; bubhuje — enjoyed; bhagavan — Bhagavan; tatra — there; sheshan — the remnants; bhrityaya — to His servant; dattavan — gave.

25There Bhagavan partook of the milk and betel offered by Srivasa, accepted the garland and incense, and gave the remnants to His servant.

Verse 26

श्रीवासभ्रातृतनयाभर्तृका मधुरद्युतिः।
प्राप्य हरेः प्रसादं च रौति नारायणी शुभा॥२६॥

śrīvāsabhrātṛtanayābhartṛkā madhuradyutiḥ|
prāpya hareḥ prasādaṁ ca rauti nārāyaṇī śubhā||26||

shrivasa-bhratri-tanaya — the daughter of Srivasa's brother; abhartrika — as yet unmarried; madhura-dyutih — sweetly radiant; prapya — receiving; hareh — of Hari; prasadam — the grace (the remnants); cha — and; rauti — weeps; narayani — Narayani; shubha — the fair.

26And the fair Narayani14, the sweetly radiant daughter of Srivasa's brother, as yet unmarried, received the remnants of Hari's meal and wept.

Verse 27

इति सकलनिशां निनाय देवो
निजजनमनसां मुदे मुरारिः।
क्षणमिव महद्वत्सरेण मेने-
ऽनवरतं सुखमापुरार्यवर्याः॥२७॥

iti sakalaniśāṁ nināya devo
nijajanamanasāṁ mude murāriḥ|
kṣaṇamiva mahadvatsareṇa mene-
'navarataṁ sukhamāpurāryavaryāḥ||27||

iti — thus; sakala-nisham — the whole night; ninaya — spent; devah — the Lord; nija-jana-manasam — of the hearts of His own people; mude — for the joy; murarih — Murari; kshanam iva — as a moment; mahat-vatsarena — (a span) equal to a great year; mene — considered; anavaratam — unbroken; sukham — happiness; apuh — attained; arya-varyah — the best of the noble.

27Thus the Lord Murari15 spent the whole night for the joy of the hearts of His own; a span as long as a great year He deemed a moment16 — and the best of the noble enjoyed unbroken happiness.

Thus ends the seventh sarga, "Grace to the Devotees" (Bhakta-anugraha), of the second prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. The text of this verse is partly damaged; the translation follows the general sense.
  2. Harihara: literally "Hari-Hara"; here, judging by the singular, an epithet of Gaura. It does not make Shiva (Hara) equal to Vishnu. Cf. 2.6.27.
  3. Gopinatha is a brahmana of Navadvipa, a companion of the Lord.
  4. Verses 10–17 are the "Ramashtaka," the eight verses of Murari Gupta, a devotee of Rama.
  5. Brihaspati and Kavi (Shukra) are the planets Jupiter and Venus.
  6. The lotus is called "hundred-petalled" (shatapatra); Sita's five fingers appear as five more petals.
  7. Lakshmana is a descent of Shesha (Ananta), the serpent on whom Vishnu reclines.
  8. Rama protected the sacrifice of the sage Vishvamitra, a descendant of Kushika, from the rakshasas Maricha and Subahu.
  9. A pun: adushana means both "undefiled" and "without Dushana" (a rakshasa, Khara's brother). Trishiras and Kabandha are rakshasas of the Dandaka forest; Sugriva's enemy is Valin; the Ten-headed is Ravana.
  10. Pinaka is Shiva's bow; the lord of the Bhargavas is Parashurama; the father is King Dasharatha.
  11. Ramadasa means "servant of Rama."
  12. Murari addresses his listener, Damodara Pandita.
  13. Bhagavata Purana 11.14.20.
  14. Narayani, Srivasa's niece, later became the mother of Vrindavana Dasa Thakura, author of the Chaitanya-bhagavata.
  15. Murari ("Enemy of Mura") is a name of Krishna; here it is Gauranga Himself, not Murari Gupta, the author of the poem.
  16. The sense of the line is unclear; the translation is tentative.
